payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully

decision.question: Is the woman's jacket fully closed in the edited image, with its front panels meeting or overlapping throughout the full intended closure?
decision.criteria: Identify the intended front closure and inspect its upper, middle, and lower portions wherever visible. Pass only if visible evidence establishes continuous meeting or overlap of the front panels throughout the full intended closure, with no unclosed segment. Fail if any clearly visible segment of that closure remains open, even if other segments are obscured or closed. Unknown if no open segment is established but pose, drape, occlusion, or insufficient detail prevents establishing full closure. Outward-hanging fabric, folds, a loose hem, changed silhouette, or absence of a clearly visible gap alone establishes neither full closure nor an open segment.
decision.binding: Use the woman's jacket in the SOURCE image as the garment reference and assess that same jacket in the EDITED image against the requested fully closed state. Locate the source jacket's front-panel edges and intended closure extent, then compare corresponding garment features and inspect any visible portions of the front-panel meeting line in the edited image, accounting for the changed pose. Do not substitute the outer silhouette for closure evidence. Unrelated changes do not satisfy this condition.
